models.title: LIFO inventory reserve
models.summary: The LIFO reserve is the difference between FIFO and reported LIFO inventory carrying amounts.

relationship.original_equation: LIFO reserve = FIFO inventory - LIFO inventory
relationship.translation_notes: The FIFO adjustment fifo=lifo+reserve is the inverse of this definition, not a separate relationship.

models.title: FIFO cost of sales from LIFO cost and reserve changes
models.summary: FIFO cost of sales is LIFO cost of sales less the change in the reserve.

relationship.original_equation: FIFO cost of sales = LIFO cost of sales - change in LIFO reserve
relationship.translation_notes: Reserve change is ending less beginning and may be negative. This relation adjusts expense, not inventory balance.

variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship
Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship
Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: The reserve uses FIFO inventory less LIFO inventory at both period endpoints.
Inventory costs and other adjustments match the same entity, reporting period and scope.
limitations: Inventory write-downs, acquisitions and other reserve movements outside cost of sales require separate treatment.
A disclosed reserve can compare LIFO with a cost method other than FIFO; the comparator must be verified.

models.title: FIFO net income from LIFO income and reserve change
models.summary: The source adjusts income for the change in cost of sales and the associated tax effect.

relationship.original_equation: FIFO net income = LIFO net income + change in LIFO reserve × (1 - tax rate)
relationship.translation_notes: The rate is a base-one fraction. The reserve is FIFO less LIFO; a fall is negative.

assumptions: Only the inventory cost-flow assumption changes and the indicated effective tax rate applies to its incremental effect.
The reserve change corresponds to the same reporting period and entity.
limitations: This is a hypothetical comparable accounting adjustment; it does not claim the company actually changed methods or taxes paid.
Complex tax effects, valuation allowances and unrelated reserve movements require further reconciliation.
